pages.title: THE GRANDVIEW GAZETTE
pages.text: $(bold)Vol. 47, No. 312$()$(br2)A 38-year-old Grandview woman was arrested yesterday after police discovered what officers described as "a scene of significant concern" in her Pine Street residence.$(br2)The welfare check was prompted by neighbors who reported a persistent odor emanating from the home for over a week.

pages.title: Investigation Details
pages.text: Officers found evidence of what the department described as "unlawful handling of human remains."$(br2)Neighbors described the suspect as "sweet" and "always bringing food to the block parties."$(br2)Her single statement to officers: $(italic)"Better have a full stomach before the snow falls!"$()

pages.title: The Casserole
pages.text: One neighbor, who asked to remain anonymous, told the Gazette:$(br2)$(italic)"She brought us a casserole last week. I ate the whole thing. I've been trying not to think about that."$()$(br2)Remains of at least two individuals were found in a basement chest freezer.

pages.title: Charges & Context
pages.text: The suspect has been charged with two counts of abuse of a corpse and one count of second-degree murder.$(br2)She was formerly employed as a line cook at the Grandview Diner, which closed in October due to "challenging operating conditions."$(br2)Sources within the DA's office privately questioned whether the court system would still be operational by spring.$(br2)Temperatures in Grandview have not risen above -20°F in six weeks.
